title: Locked Doors
story: Three locked permission doors inside `~/doors/` and a root-owned vault at `/opt/vault/flag.txt` stand between you and the flag. Master `ls -l`, `chmod`, and `sudo -l` to open every door.
objective:
1. Door 1: `~/doors/door1.txt` has mode `000` (Permission denied). Make it readable with `chmod u+r ~/doors/door1.txt`.
2. Door 2: `~/doors/unlock.sh` is not executable. Run `chmod +x ~/doors/unlock.sh` and execute `~/doors/unlock.sh`.
3. Door 3: Set `~/doors/door3.key` permissions to **exactly** `640` (`rw-r-----`) using `chmod 640 ~/doors/door3.key`.
4. The Vault: Run `sudo -l` to see which command you are allowed to run as `root`, run `sudo /usr/bin/cat /opt/vault/flag.txt`, save the `VAULT_SECRET=...` line into `~/doors/vault.txt`, and run `quest check`.
hints: Run `sudo -l` to see the exact allowed command (`sudo /usr/bin/cat /opt/vault/flag.txt`), copy the `VAULT_SECRET=...` value into `~/doors/vault.txt`, and run `quest check`.
